name: Aloo Paratha
summary: Flatbreads stuffed with spiced mashed potato and pan-fried, served with butter and plain yogurt. Two per person.

ingredients.name: chili powder (or cayenne for more heat)
vegetable oil (for the dough and the pan)

instructions: Mix the flour, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp oil, and about 250 mL water into a soft dough. Knead 3 minutes and rest it covered while you make the filling.
Boil the potatoes 15 minutes until soft. Drain well and mash with the onion, cumin, garam masala, chili, and 1 tsp salt. Let cool so it is easy to handle.
Divide the dough and filling into 8 portions each. Flatten a dough ball into a 10 cm circle, put a ball of filling in the centre, pull the edges up to seal, and press flat.
Dust with flour and gently roll each into an 18 cm round. Some filling peeking out is fine.
Cook in a dry, hot skillet 1 minute per side, then brush with oil and fry 1–2 minutes more per side until golden spots appear. Serve with butter and yogurt.

substitutions.substitute: skip the dough: mix 3 tbsp cornstarch into the potato filling, shape into 12 patties (aloo tikki), and pan-fry in oil until crisp. Serve with the yogurt and rice
substitutions.costNote: Cornstarch costs about $0.10. Adding 300 g rice ($0.75) keeps it under $6

glutenFree.notes: The potato filling, yogurt, and butter are naturally gluten-free. Wheat flour is the only source of gluten.

budgetNotes: The most involved recipe in this set, but the ingredients cost under $5 for four people.
If rolling stuffed breads is too fussy, roll plain dough thin and fold the filling inside like a quesadilla.
The filling must be fully cooled and fairly dry, or it will tear through the dough.
